DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The combination of fluctuating double vision, proximal muscle weakness affecting your stairs, and upper limb weakness, alongside the positive antibody markers and thyroid workup, strongly points to this neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend proceeding with an acetylcholine receptor antibody titration and considering a trial of pyridostigmine to confirm the diagnosis.
